topic: Interactive Planning Protocol: task complexity tiers
idea: System prompt classifies each request Simple/Complex/Agentic and scales reasoning depth: simple = direct tool call, complex = CoT template in <thinking>, agentic = multi-phase template (solution-space exploration, trade-offs, validation criteria, implementation plan, synthesis).
does: AI Mode prompt routes a request to a reasoning template by complexity, saving tokens on simple asks and forcing trade-off and validation planning on open goals.
outputs: tier + template injected into the prompt
existing: partial: note_plan (goal, hypothesis, plan, expectation, conclusion)
notes: ACMS note_plan is a structured plan record, but no tiering of depth.

topic: Parameter sufficiency validation against a scenario schema
idea: Each request is mapped to a scenario schema (spatial scope, demand/OD, policy interventions, experimental design, evaluation metrics); if any critical field is missing the agent pauses and asks structured clarification questions with recommended defaults and explicit assumptions, resuming only when confirmed.
does: Before run_experiment/build_scenario, check that the plan fills the 5 schema slots (scope, demand, intervention, seeds/design, KPIs) and return the missing ones with default proposals.
outputs: list of missing slots, proposed defaults, assumptions
notes: Could be validation inside note_plan itself.

idea: Before running, agent summarises the plan (inputs, steps, expected outputs, validation checks) and waits for explicit user confirmation; simple tasks with sufficient parameters proceed directly with documented assumptions.
does: Gate expensive tools (multi-seed experiments) behind a user-visible plan preview and approval; log assumptions.
existing: partial: note_plan; edits are proposed then applied or skipped
notes: ACMS has apply-or-skip for network edits, not for experiments.

topic: Simulation state dictionary injected as XML context
idea: A state dict records artifacts generated in the session (network, routes, results); before a new request the agent checks whether they exist to avoid re-generation, and the state is injected into the next system prompt as XML.
does: Inject a compact summary of what exists (open network, demand, last runs, last experiments with seeds) into every prompt so the LLM does not regenerate or re-run; cache identical (network, demand, seed) runs.
existing: partial: network_summary, read_results, compare_runs (pull, not pushed)

topic: Prompt caching of static prompt and tool definitions
idea: Static sections of the system prompt and tool schemas are cached across turns to cut latency and cost in multi-turn planning.
does: Mark the static prefix (docs, tool list) as cacheable for providers that support it; keep dynamic state at the end.
notes: 62 tools means a large schema; only some providers support caching.

idea: Seven modular policy tools: Green Wave (tlsCoordinator), Webster cycle adaptation, road closure, lane reduction, speed adjustment, vehicle generation and fleet composition change, combined in one conversation.
does: Scenario operations for what-if: close or drop N lanes on a road segment (e.g. 500 m of a road), change speed, change fleet mix, then paired run vs baseline.
inputs: road id, lanes closed, segment length, time window
notes: Check whether build_scenario supports partial-length or timed lane closures. Green wave is covered by TRANSYT/Synchro offsets.

idea: Compare strategies on network-wide density, top-10 congested edges, and density within 300 m and 500 m of a point of interest (Table 4): green wave cut network density 16.5 to 12.9 veh/km, MSG area 73.3 to 51.9, top-10 edges about 45%. Lane closure also reported road occupancy 58.95% to 67.92%.
does: KPIs of a run restricted to a radius around a junction or institution and for the top-N congested links, for before/after comparison.
outputs: mean density/speed within each radius; top-N link densities

idea: Event dispersal: capacity 20,000, 10% by car = 2,000 vehicles, 3 origins, 9 destination gateways, 60% depart in first 30 min and 40% spread over the rest; baseline plus event flows, find hotspots, then test mitigation (Table 3, Fig 8).
does: Template tool adding a time-profiled burst of OD demand from a venue/institution to boundary ends with a front-loaded egress split, then baseline vs event vs mitigation runs.
inputs: venue, attendance, car share, egress split %, window min, destinations
notes: ACMS notes a what-if cannot add institution trips since demand is fixed before scenarios; a burst needs time-windowed demand.

idea: Sweep fleet share of EVs 0/25/50/75/100%, report CO2, NOx, PMx, fuel, electricity per trip and by edge; PMx fell 73% at 75% EV.
does: Per-vehicle emission and energy accounting and a fleet-share sweep.
inputs: vehicle types with emission class, share sweep
notes: SUMO uses HBEFA classes; ACMS has no emissions. Would need a simple speed/acceleration emission model not given in the paper.

idea: Simulation outputs (tripinfo, edgeData, summary) loaded into SQLite via an MCP server for querying and cross-scenario comparison; JSON with semantic labels.
does: Let the assistant query across stored runs (stdlib sqlite3) by scenario, seed, KPI.

topic: Agent evaluation by task tiers with KPI sanity checks
idea: Evaluation = three tiers (simple generation at light/medium/heavy, complex paired policy tests, agentic open-ended event) with sanity check that KPIs scale with demand; no baseline agents, seeds or significance tests.
does: A suite of prompt tasks per tier with expected tool-call traces and monotonicity checks on KPIs, to regression-test AI Mode.
notes: AgentSUMO is weak on rigour: single runs. ACMS (seeds, paired t-tests) is stronger.

idea: Tools are stateless functions whose signature and docstring become the JSON schema; the description tells the LLM when to use the tool; host/client/server separation, runtime discovery.
does: Expose ACMS TOOLS over MCP stdio so external agents can drive the app.
notes: The mcp package breaks the no-dependency rule; raw JSON-RPC over stdio would be small.
